lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eIon–ion\u003c/b\u003e: "Ion–ion 1/r, ion–dipole 1/r², dipole–dipole 1/r³: the smaller the exponent, the longer the range."
lit.\u0027\u003cb\u003eLondon\u003c/b\u003e: "London acts between all molecules (∝ r⁻⁶) and grows with polarizability."
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eDos moléculas de \u00:
"

Two HCl molecules: in the head-to-tail arrangement (δ+ facing δ−) they attract; head-to-head (δ−/δ−) they repel. The energy depends on the orientation and falls as 1/r³ if the molecules are fixed (r⁻⁶ when they rotate freely: Keesom).

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn \u003cb\u003eCF₃I\:
"

In CF₃I iodine presents a positive zone (σ-hole) opposite the C–I bond that attracts a lone pair: halogen bond (≈ −13 kJ/mol), very directional (C–I···O ≈ 180°). In benzene, the quadrupole and dispersion favor displaced π–π stacking.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEntre \u003cb\u003eNa:
"

Between Na⁺ and Cl⁻ the Coulomb energy decays as 1/r and reaches ≈ −500 kJ/mol. An ion facing a polar molecule (Na⁺···H₂O) orients the dipole toward the charge: U ∝ 1/r² and ≈ −100 kJ/mol. It is the basis of ion hydration.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEntre átomos de \u003:
"

Between argon atoms there are no permanent charges or dipoles, but the electron cloud fluctuates and generates an instantaneous dipole that induces another in the neighbor. The attraction (London, ∝ r⁻⁶) exists between all molecules and grows with polarizability. At short distance Pauli repulsion (∝ r⁻¹²) dominates: the result is the Lennard-Jones well.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eProfundidad del pozo:
"

Well depth in this model: Ar···Ar ≈ −1 kJ/mol, HCl···HCl ≈ −4, H₂O···H₂O ≈ −27, HCOOH···HCOOH ≈ −52 and Na⁺···Cl⁻ ≈ −500 kJ/mol. Compared with kBT ≈ 2.5 kJ/mol (298 K), they explain why some substances are gases and others ionic solids.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eUn H unido a un átomo:
"

An H bonded to a very electronegative atom (O, N, F) interacts with a lone pair of another: H₂O···H₂O (≈ −27 kJ/mol) and the cyclic dimer of formic acid with two bonds (≈ −52 kJ/mol). The interaction is directional (≈ 180° at X–H···A) and the H···A distance ≈ 1.8–2.0 Å.

"

lit.\u0027Activa el promedio térmico y sube: 'Turn on the thermal average and raise T: dipole–dipole attraction weakens (Keesom ∝ 1/T).'
lit.\u0027Átomos esféricos y neutros: no hay: "Spherical, neutral atoms: no charge or permanent dipole. There is only the attraction due to correlated instantaneous dipoles, balanced by Pauli repulsion at short range. Very shallow well."
lit.\u0027Atracción de Coulomb entre cargas: "Coulomb attraction between full charges (∝ 1/r): the one with the longest range and energy. Pauli repulsion (r⁻¹²) sets the equilibrium distance. In the crystal each ion is surrounded by six counterions."
lit.\u0027Cada agua puede donar dos puentes: "Each water can donate two H bonds and accept two others: this explains its high boiling point. Press “Relax geometry” and watch how the H of one molecule aligns toward the lone pair of the O of the other (O–H···O ≈ 180°)."
lit.\u0027carga la mejor geometría del model: "loads the best geometry of the model."
lit.\u0027CCSD(T): D\u003csub\u003ee\u003c/s: "CCSD(T): D<sub>e</sub> ≈ 10–11 kJ/mol (T and displaced) · Θ ≈ −8.7 D·Å · α′ = 10.3 Å³"
lit.\u0027CO₂ es lineal y apolar (μ = 0) per: "CO₂ is linear and nonpolar (μ = 0) but with a large quadrupole (Θ ≈ −4.3 D·Å). The preferred geometries are T-shaped and parallel displaced; the linear end-to-end one is repulsive: observe the rule of the δ+ charges of C versus δ− of O."
lit.\u0027Como el agua, el metanol dona y ac: "Like water, methanol donates and accepts, but it has only one polar H and the bulky CH₃: it forms linear chains and rings instead of a 3D network. Hence it boils at 65 °C and not at 100 °C."
lit.\u0027Compara cómo cae cada interacción: 'Compare how each interaction falls off with distance: ion–ion (1/r) reaches much further than London (1/r⁶).'
lit.\u0027Compara el pozo con \u003cb\u003ek: "Compare the well with k_BT: if it is smaller, thermal agitation separates the pair."
lit.\u0027Con carga +2 y menor radio, el Mg²: "With +2 charge and smaller radius, Mg²⁺ polarizes and orients water much more than Na⁺: that is why its hydration shell is so stable and its water exchange is slow."
lit.\u0027Dímero experimental: O···O ≈ 2,98: "Experimental dimer: O···O ≈ 2.98 Å, D<sub>e</sub> ≈ 21 kJ/mol. The TIP3P model (designed for liquid) gives O···O ≈ 2.75 Å and ≈ 27 kJ/mol."
lit.\u0027Dipolos permanentes que giran libr: "Freely rotating permanent dipoles interact according to…"
lit.\u0027Dos ácidos carboxílicos forman un: "Two carboxylic acids form an eight-membered ring with two O–H···O=C bonds. It is the most stable dimer of those listed and persists even in the gas phase and in nonpolar solvents. Press “Relax geometry” to find the cyclic form."
lit.\u0027Dos cationes se repelen a cualquie: "Two cations repel at any distance: the curve is always positive and decays slowly (1/r). To form an ionic solid, counterions are needed to offset this repulsion."
lit.\u0027El agua actúa como donor y el N de: "Water acts as the donor and the N of ammonia as the acceptor, which is the preferred direction: the O–H is more acidic than the N–H. Try the opposite orientation to compare them."
lit.\u0027El agua también puede ser aceptor: "Water can also be a halogen-bond acceptor through the lone pair of the O. The strong directional character (±15°) is what distinguishes this bond from a simple dispersion interaction."
lit.\u0027El anillo aromático actúa como ace: "The aromatic ring acts as a weak H-bond acceptor: an O–H of water points toward the π cloud (negative face). It is weaker than an O–H···O bond but directional."
lit.\u0027El anión se acerca al extremo posi: "The anion approaches the positive end of water (the H atoms): water orients with an O–H pointing at the anion, forming an ion–dipole hydrogen bond. Illustrative ionic parameters."
lit.\u0027El campo del catión deforma la nub: "The cation's field distorts the Ar cloud and induces a dipole (magenta arrow) oriented toward the ion: U<sub>ind</sub> = −½ α′ q²/(4πε₀) / r⁴. It falls off faster than ion–permanent dipole but slower than London. Turn off “Induction” to see what is left with repulsion + dispersion only."
lit.\u0027El campo del dipolo del HCl polari: "The field of the HCl dipole polarizes Ar. The induction (Debye) contribution is independent of T and of sign, always attractive, but small compared with dispersion. You will see the magenta arrow on Ar."
lit.\u0027El catión interacciona con los O (: "The cation interacts with the O atoms (δ−) through the quadrupolar part of CO₂; in the linear geometry the attraction is strong, in the T it is repulsive. It is the basis of CO₂ capture in zeolites with cations."
lit.\u0027El catión se coloca sobre la cara: "The cation sits over the negative face of the ring: interaction with the quadrupole plus induction of the highly polarizable π cloud. It is the basis of cation recognition (K⁺, NH₄⁺) by proteins with aromatic rings."
lit.\u0027El CO casi no tiene momento dipola: "CO has almost no dipole moment (μ ≈ 0.11 D) despite having a polar bond. Compare with HCl: the electrostatic contribution is minimal compared with dispersion. Generic illustrative parameters."
lit.\u0027El dipolo del agua interacciona co: "The water dipole interacts with the CO₂ quadrupole: the water O approaches the C (δ+) and one H approaches an O of CO₂. It contributes to the solubility of CO₂ in water."
lit.\u0027El extremo negativo del dipolo del: "The negative end of the water dipole (the O) orients toward the cation. It is the basis of ion hydration and of the solubility of salts. Rotate molecule B and watch the energy change sign. Turn on “Induction” to see the contribution of the polarization of water (already included effectively in the TIP3P charges)."
lit.\u0027El gas noble estable más polarizab: "The most polarizable stable noble gas of the series: deeper well and higher boiling temperature. Compare with Ne using the selector."
lit.\u0027El grupo carbonilo es muy polar (μ: "The carbonyl group is very polar (μ(model) ≈ 2.6 D; experimental 2.33 D). Antiparallel dimers of carbonyls, with lateral displacement Δy, are the reason ketones and aldehydes have higher T<sub>b</sub> than alkanes of similar mass."
lit.\u0027El H unido al F (muy electronegati: "The H bonded to F (very electronegative) carries a high partial positive charge and is attracted to a lone pair of the neighboring F. It is the most directional: the maximum energy is achieved with the F–H···F angle close to 180°. In this model the force is due to Coulomb; reality includes some charge transfer."
lit.\u0027El I tiene una región positiva en: "I has a positive region along the extension of the C–I bond (σ-hole, light-blue sphere) and a negative belt on the sides. A Lewis base (N lone pair) sits on the axis with C–I···N ≈ 180°: just like a hydrogen bond, but with a halogen as the density acceptor."
lit.\u0027El N es menos electronegativo que: "N is less electronegative than O: weaker bonds and only one lone pair per molecule; that is why NH₃ boils much lower than H₂O (−33 °C) despite being isoelectronic."
lit.\u0027El O carbonílico es un excelente a: "The carbonyl O is an excellent acceptor: water positions itself with an O–H pointing at the lone pair of the C=O. This is how ketones, aldehydes and amides, and the C=O groups of the protein backbone, are hydrated."
lit.\u0027El promedio de Boltzmann sobre ori: "The Boltzmann average over orientations gives an r⁻⁶ term that decreases with T."
lit.\u0027El Xe es más polarizable que el Ar: "Xe is more polarizable than Ar (α′ = 4.04 Å³): the induced dipole is larger and so is the dispersion. Compare with HCl···Ar the “induction” column and the total depth of the well."
lit.\u0027Elige un par en «Lab», ajusta dist: "Choose a pair in “Lab”, adjust the distance and orientations, and compare U with k_BT."
lit.\u0027En un gas las moléculas giran: los: "In a gas the molecules rotate: the dipoles orient according to the Boltzmann weight and the average decays as r⁻⁶ and as 1/T (Keesom): U = −(2/3) μ⁴ / [(4πε₀)² k<sub>B</sub>T r⁶]. The dotted line is that point-dipole formula; raise the temperature and you will see the average well become shallower."
lit.\u0027Es la base de la solubilidad de ga: "It is the basis of the solubility of noble gases and of O₂/N₂ in water: the large dipole of water polarizes the neighboring nonpolar molecule and attracts it."
lit.\u0027Escala log–log: la pendiente es el: "Log–log scale: the slope is the exponent of r. Pink line: k_BT at 298 K."
lit.\u0027Este simulador trata pares aislado: "This simulator treats isolated pairs; the hydrophobic effect is a property of the liquid (solvent + entropy)."
lit.\u0027Existe entre todas las moléculas y: "It exists between all molecules and grows with α′ (which is why Xe boils at a higher T than Ne)."
lit.\u0027Experimental (fase gas): ≈ 100–120: "Experimental (gas phase): ≈ 100–120 kJ/mol; this model overestimates. Illustrative parameters."

lit.\u0027Igual que con el catión, pero el d: "Same as with the cation, but the induced dipole points the opposite way: the induction energy does not depend on the sign of the charge (∝ q²). The well is shallower because Cl⁻ is much larger and the repulsion keeps it farther away."

The “hydrophobic effect” is not a pairwise repulsion but a collective effect: water loses entropy on structuring itself around the solute, and that is why nonpolar molecules cluster together."

lit.\u0027La energía es proporcional al prod: "The energy is proportional to the product q₁q₂: with a divalent cation the attraction doubles relative to Na⁺···Cl⁻ and the well is much deeper (higher lattice energy of MgCl₂ than of NaCl)."

lit.\u0027Mayor tamaño de nube ⇒ mayor polar: "Larger electron cloud ⇒ greater polarizability ⇒ stronger instantaneous dipoles and a deeper well than in Ar."
